judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 1205, requiring every paid or volunteer petition collector to register, live in Florida, be a United States citizen, and lack an unrestored felony. Invalid collectors' forms do not count; holding over 25 outside family is a third-degree felony; delivery drops from 30 days to 10 with $2,500 fines; forms need ID digits; voters get mailed verification and prepaid fraud-revocation forms. Invalidity over one-quarter triggers investigation, the RICO racketeering law may cover fraud, committees get one initiative, proposals expire after three elections below 25 percent, and state ads are barred; the House changed the Senate rewrite and passed it 81-30 into law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for CS/HB 1205, accepting the last House change and completing passage. The law rewrote Florida's rules for citizen petitions to amend the state constitution. Every petition circulator, paid or volunteer, must register with the state and be a Florida resident and citizen. People with felony convictions may not circulate petitions unless their voting rights are restored. An unregistered person holding more than 25 signed forms, beyond their own and their immediate family's, commits a third-degree felony. Sponsors must deliver signed forms within 10 days instead of 30, with fines up to $2,500 for a late form. Signers must add a driver license number, state ID number, or the last four Social Security digits. Election officials mail each signer a notice, which the signer can use to cancel a forged signature. A sponsor may run only one amendment at a time. Petition fraud can be charged under Florida's racketeering law. The state may not spend public money on ads about proposed amendments. The Senate agreed 28-9 and the governor signed it as Chapter 2025-21.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against CS/HB 1205 at the vote that completed its passage. The bill tightened Florida's citizen petition process for amending the state constitution. All petition circulators must register with the state and be Florida residents and citizens. An unregistered person holding more than 25 signed forms, beyond their own and their immediate family's, commits a third-degree felony. The deadline to turn in signed forms dropped from 30 days to 10, with fines up to $2,500 per late form. Signers must add a driver license number, state ID number, or the last four Social Security digits. A sponsor may run only one amendment at a time, and petition fraud can be charged as racketeering. The state may no longer pay for ads about proposed amendments. The Senate agreed 28-9 and it became law as Chapter 2025-21.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 700, a 92-section agriculture package. Water additives must meet drinking standards, remove pollutants, or improve water, ending dental fluoride used in about 29 counties; a local-choice amendment failed 13-21. It protects verified farmworker housing, gives the state first chance to buy utility farmland, controls charger permits, registers public chargers, bans some drones, and lists charities free of money or direction from hostile foreign sources. The Florida Senate passed it 27-9, and it became law.
